Do not return hashes; the host binds immutable hashes.", "context": {"title": "David Copperfield", "unit": 16, "heading": "CHAPTER 14. MY AUNT MAKES UP HER MIND ABOUT ME", "previous_rows": [{"source_id": "en85-u016-b0062", "target": "— Да, дитя, — сказала тётка, снова потирая нос. — Он подаёт прошение лорду-канцлеру, или лорду как-его-там, — словом, одному из тех людей, которым платят за то, чтобы им подавали прошения, — о своих делах. Полагаю, оно когда-нибудь будет подано. Пока что он не смог составить его, не вводя этот способ выражения; но это неважно: это его занимает.", "source_sha256": "480bbcff90def4f0a2085b5f965a93abfe1c1b343403e11789925c0adc9ea5b7", "target_id": "ru-en85-u016-b0062", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "327c38569db4b8a7a37aa1ebf3fa4d9a8bb009519437beed7c3954692937253b"}, {"source_id": "en85-u016-b0063", "target": "В самом деле, позже я узнал, что мистер Дик уже более десяти лет старался не допустить короля Карла Первого в Прошение; но тот постоянно в него попадал и находился там и теперь.", "source_sha256": "29c0a0270cda73f059336336e353c6f2e73f955c2d9164824a2d4b67a40dc7c6", "target_id": "ru-en85-u016-b0063", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "fd420d37647e726520b78179b7f94d463264783e27f6510e593f686607ad9603"}], "source_language": "English", "part": null, "book": null, "chapter": 14, "role": "chapter"}, "source_rows": [{"id": "en85-u016-b0064", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I say again,’ said my aunt, ‘nobody knows what that man’s mind is except myself; and he’s the most amenable and friendly creature in existence. If he likes to fly a kite sometimes, what of that! Franklin used to fly a kite. He was a Quaker, or something of that sort, if I am not mistaken. And a Quaker flying a kite is a much more ridiculous object than anybody else.’", "sha256": "05c9ebf6397c480f8c4c07455813b21c3ea2a2bd8bd4ba63d1d0697c1c1badee", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[21]/p[64]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u016-b0065", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "If I could have supposed that my aunt had recounted these particulars for my especial behoof, and as a piece of confidence in me, I should have felt very much distinguished, and should have augured favourably from such a mark of her good opinion. But I could hardly help observing that she had launched into them, chiefly because the question was raised in her own mind, and with very little reference to me, though she had addressed herself to me in the absence of anybody else.", "sha256": "0d88135c724b02c2a6a57e0864de7f4d6b34869ee7046f29d38839826906b0e3", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[21]/p[65]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u016-b0066", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "At the same time, I must say that the generosity of her championship of poor harmless Mr. Dick, not only inspired my young breast with some selfish hope for myself, but warmed it unselfishly towards her. I believe that I began to know that there was something about my aunt, notwithstanding her many eccentricities and odd humours, to be honoured and trusted in. Though she was just as sharp that day as on the day before, and was in and out about the donkeys just as often, and was thrown into a tremendous state of indignation, when a young man, going by, ogled Janet at a window (which was one of the gravest misdemeanours that could be committed against my aunt’s dignity), she seemed to me to command more of my respect, if not less of my fear.", "sha256": "e27153e8361ee2d63148815c703be6edf5cf4037ed0745ed5d6211a0a3aaf4bf", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[21]/p[66]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u016-b0067", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "The anxiety I underwent, in the interval which necessarily elapsed before a reply could be received to her letter to Mr. Murdstone, was extreme; but I made an endeavour to suppress it, and to be as agreeable as I could in a quiet way, both to my aunt and Mr. Dick. The latter and I would have gone out to fly the great kite; but that I had still no other clothes than the anything but ornamental garments with which I had been decorated on the first day, and which confined me to the house, except for an hour after dark, when my aunt, for my health’s sake, paraded me up and down on the cliff outside, before going to bed. At length the reply from Mr. Murdstone came, and my aunt informed me, to my infinite terror, that he was coming to speak to her herself on the next day. On the next day, still bundled up in my curious habiliments, I sat counting the time, flushed and heated by the conflict of sinking hopes and rising fears within me; and waiting to be startled by the sight of the gloomy face, whose non-arrival startled me every minute.", "sha256": "0b44c6ebde4d7dd618f596580e80e34ea4e73d745fdb798746a6411f3f675351", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[21]/p[67]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u016-b0068", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "My aunt was a little more imperious and stern than usual, but I observed no other token of her preparing herself to receive the visitor so much dreaded by me. She sat at work in the window, and I sat by, with my thoughts running astray on all possible and impossible results of Mr. Murdstone’s visit, until pretty late in the afternoon. Our dinner had been indefinitely postponed; but it was growing so late, that my aunt had ordered it to be got ready, when she gave a sudden alarm of donkeys, and to my consternation and amazement, I beheld Miss Murdstone, on a side-saddle, ride deliberately over the sacred piece of green, and stop in front of the house, looking about her.", "sha256": "64887a4815fb405436fdcdbae5a81ad56cfc3dfe0cd67bd3d839345c2c1a18e4", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[21]/p[68]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u016-b0069", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Go along with you!’ cried my aunt, shaking her head and her fist at the window. ‘You have no business there. How dare you trespass? Go along! Oh! you bold-faced thing!’", "sha256": "25e94cef820ca9ee2dd982f449845421aa270d5cab59c1394d445058037ad8fa", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[21]/p[69]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u016-b0070", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "My aunt was so exasperated by the coolness with which Miss Murdstone looked about her, that I really believe she was motionless, and unable for the moment to dart out according to custom. I seized the opportunity to inform her who it was; and that the gentleman now coming near the offender (for the way up was very steep, and he had dropped behind), was Mr. Murdstone himself.", "sha256": "ebc7101e2775df038ec477fbde9fe6b712554ff824c6878b83009c217dd432cd", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[21]/p[70]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u016-b0071", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I don’t care who it is!’ cried my aunt, still shaking her head and gesticulating anything but welcome from the bow-window. ‘I won’t be trespassed upon. I won’t allow it. Go away! Janet, turn him round. Lead him off!’ and I saw, from behind my aunt, a sort of hurried battle-piece, in which the donkey stood resisting everybody, with all his four legs planted different ways, while Janet tried to pull him round by the bridle, Mr. Murdstone tried to lead him on, Miss Murdstone struck at Janet with a parasol, and several boys, who had come to see the engagement, shouted vigorously. But my aunt, suddenly descrying among them the young malefactor who was the donkey’s guardian, and who was one of the most inveterate offenders against her, though hardly in his teens, rushed out to the scene of action, pounced upon him, captured him, dragged him, with his jacket over his head, and his heels grinding the ground, into the garden, and, calling upon Janet to fetch the constables and justices, that he might be taken, tried, and executed on the spot, held him at bay there. This part of the business, however, did not last long; for the young rascal, being expert at a variety of feints and dodges, of which my aunt had no conception, soon went whooping away, leaving some deep impressions of his nailed boots in the flower-beds, and taking his donkey in triumph with him.", "sha256": "d2a9347890f826924fbbfe1473a8a9e4889a19a717fc49d33f0aad74c97f183f", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[21]/p[71]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u016-b0072", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Miss Murdstone, during the latter portion of the contest, had dismounted, and was now waiting with her brother at the bottom of the steps, until my aunt should be at leisure to receive them. My aunt, a little ruffled by the combat, marched past them into the house, with great dignity, and took no notice of their presence, until they were announced by Janet.", "sha256": "a895c637f2adfe8358615a0eaa6e3a8da58ab748d4a0fc7e042c1e0c4b7ac8d9", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[21]/p[72]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u016-b0073", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Shall I go away, aunt?’ I asked, trembling.", "sha256": "743a22db7183552768c8f8a9a3f96e23bb7e511821438173dbad5c509c4e19dc", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[21]/p[73]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u016-b0074", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘No, sir,’ said my aunt. ‘Certainly not!’ With which she pushed me into a corner near her, and fenced Me in with a chair, as if it were a prison or a bar of justice. This position I continued to occupy during the whole interview, and from it I now saw Mr. and Miss Murdstone enter the room.", "sha256": "32084e5ef0cd00717f9b9d0610f7197a2a6901fb5a9af76ba1f27a25556d761e", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[21]/p[74]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u016-b0075", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Oh!’ said my aunt, ‘I was not aware at first to whom I had the pleasure of objecting. But I don’t allow anybody to ride over that turf. I make no exceptions. I don’t allow anybody to do it.’", "sha256": "f01ad8a4efa23f37a21f974b3b7cced212f53bf2dcf758dade6e8d764153e435", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[21]/p[75]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u016-b0076", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Your regulation is rather awkward to strangers,’ said Miss Murdstone.", "sha256": "fc2926ffefe794bc0b65bcf46495b3dfc13698c735e946247d19ea35ebd5ba47", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[21]/p[76]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u016-b0077", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Is it!’ said my aunt.", "sha256": "290366f43407e05f8d928c97537275de68ec3e03aff8cc18fb7daa4b49c90af4", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[21]/p[77]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u016-b0078", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Mr. Murdstone seemed afraid of a renewal of hostilities, and interposing began:", "sha256": "26a016aae9d54f82708f9276f892561ac13280644cfe667c4e0d40ca5cc9d5c8", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[21]/p[78]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u016-b0079", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Miss Trotwood!’", "sha256": "ce00400c99d0c413d2f56abb2bc4957c1a412a70c6359d4ea0a6fb063ac14d7c", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[21]/p[79]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u016-b0080", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I beg your pardon,’ observed my aunt with a keen look. ‘You are the Mr. Murdstone who married the widow of my late nephew, David Copperfield, of Blunderstone Rookery!—Though why Rookery, I don’t know!’", "sha256": "82a38a176fe458dd49ff00f43dbd8d2d843ad81ff9b2bc5a4da89e2e21f28871", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[21]/p[80]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u016-b0081", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I am,’ said Mr. Murdstone.", "sha256": "874e95de56cff6b7ed3eb9daf0d4f7df47d5f8e29a02a05250af9e19208c5a05", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[21]/p[81]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u016-b0082", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘You’ll excuse my saying, sir,’ returned my aunt, ‘that I think it would have been a much better and happier thing if you had left that poor child alone.’", "sha256": "1c383d1be15e990f835c84bc74b3fc03df6aef90f4ae4ce5314846e0a3427b9c", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[21]/p[82]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u016-b0083", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I so far agree with what Miss Trotwood has remarked,’ observed Miss Murdstone, bridling, ‘that I consider our lamented Clara to have been, in all essential respects, a mere child.’", "sha256": "3a9111c3185747ae3116fbc5e002e295ade5f1652db3245ae762e1bc1e49d0d8", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[21]/p[83]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u016-b0084", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘It is a comfort to you and me, ma’am,’ said my aunt, ‘who are getting on in life, and are not likely to be made unhappy by our personal attractions, that nobody can say the same of us.’", "sha256": "9d866e632860590c9dc1cc42cf881217b6c368019e9d912d6c4c63eb82974110", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[21]/p[84]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u016-b0085", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘No doubt!’ returned Miss Murdstone, though, I thought, not with a very ready or gracious assent. ‘And it certainly might have been, as you say, a better and happier thing for my brother if he had never entered into such a marriage. I have always been of that opinion.’", "sha256": "310ce9e58fe3c5daea2a4f574866b90482949605f00f8c350ad9105b53ce7504", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[21]/p[85]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u016-b0086", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I have no doubt you have,’ said my aunt. ‘Janet,’ ringing the bell, ‘my compliments to Mr. Dick, and beg him to come down.’", "sha256": "983245fcd7f2d08ac95d4bb61ce4df38a0d4bbdf3fd8d54bb14c66a3bcbb7afb", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[21]/p[86]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u016-b0087", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Until he came, my aunt sat perfectly upright and stiff, frowning at the wall. When he came, my aunt performed the ceremony of introduction.", "sha256": "9ff424ccdabf79ac92c46e5712ce5bd271379be212bc05f30e89e70ed48ff36f", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[21]/p[87]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u016-b0088", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Mr. Dick. An old and intimate friend. On whose judgement,’ said my aunt, with emphasis, as an admonition to Mr. Dick, who was biting his forefinger and looking rather foolish, ‘I rely.’", "sha256": "0002c276eaddd1cdf1784b55f6cc53449c58362ee0eea0cc1102e737e07d5f52", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[21]/p[88]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u016-b0089", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Mr. Dick took his finger out of his mouth, on this hint, and stood among the group, with a grave and attentive expression of face.", "sha256": "830236b6387c8cf1a4a9a1b15ffa1e3a17bc96b6692ddbd7ff5fe5b85b6a9331", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[21]/p[89]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u016-b0090", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "My aunt inclined her head to Mr. Murdstone, who went on:", "sha256": "6ba7d8aaf7702a1d0209323fd9d400ed0f9ff29844f6005f41c7bd8c8f30a430", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[21]/p[90]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u016-b0091", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Miss Trotwood: on the receipt of your letter, I considered it an act of greater justice to myself, and perhaps of more respect to you—’", "sha256": "c1f1da8c6997af01909c60d1e007bb624db172656c098949247aead6aad92412", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[21]/p[91]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u016-b0092", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Thank you,’ said my aunt, still eyeing him keenly. ‘You needn’t mind me.’", "sha256": "39afb5e59b47457b8bfe0f9ccf5642bf3674bbd7974ce561dd7ca77f39adb768", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[21]/p[92]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u016-b0093", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘To answer it in person, however inconvenient the journey,’ pursued Mr. Murdstone, ‘rather than by letter. This unhappy boy who has run away from his friends and his occupation—’", "sha256": "f06f6a056ad71caa581358162164f96ca1b88a252340c3a2dda20c45252c7f94", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[21]/p[93]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u016-b0094", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘And whose appearance,’ interposed his sister, directing general attention to me in my indefinable costume, ‘is perfectly scandalous and disgraceful.’", "sha256": "f74fbaa0c1abab86d64b6348c3a2efec688f4c756b75f894337455752d71170d", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[21]/p[94]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u016-b0095", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Jane Murdstone,’ said her brother, ‘have the goodness not to interrupt me. This unhappy boy, Miss Trotwood, has been the occasion of much domestic trouble and uneasiness; both during the lifetime of my late dear wife, and since. He has a sullen, rebellious spirit; a violent temper; and an untoward, intractable disposition. Both my sister and myself have endeavoured to correct his vices, but ineffectually. And I have felt—we both have felt, I may say; my sister being fully in my confidence—that it is right you should receive this grave and dispassionate assurance from our lips.’", "sha256": "bd12c7f1c46dff2af7401ab7e3303c7f23f46f67faa4207c3451c7d0addb9fd1", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[21]/p[95]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}]}
